title: Clarify data retention + residency language (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) + add glossary
author: Kira Thompson
description:
## Context
Enterprise security reviews have repeatedly flagged ambiguity in our docs around (a) what we mean by “data retention” (prompt/response vs logs vs backups), and (b) what “data residency” applies to in each deployment mode. Sales/SEs have been linking customers to the docs site and then needing to walk back interpretations during questionnaires.

This PR tightens language to be more precise and deployment-mode-specific (Hosted / Dedicated / Private), adds explicit caveats we already follow in practice, and introduces a glossary that aligns with the internal Security FAQ phrasing. This is a wording/structure update only; no product behavior changes and no roadmap commitments.

## What changed
- Rewrote the “Data retention” section to split content into:
  - Customer Content (prompt/response payloads)
  - Derived Data (embeddings/rerank inputs where applicable)
  - Operational Metadata (request IDs, timestamps, model, token counts)
  - Security/Access Audit Logs
  - Backups & disaster recovery copies (where applicable)
- Added deployment-mode tables:
  - Hosted: clarifies what is configurable vs fixed, and distinguishes content handling from operational metadata.
  - Dedicated: clarifies isolation boundary and what may still be present in Redwood-managed control-plane metadata.
  - Private: clarifies customer-managed storage/logging boundaries and that residency is governed by customer environment.
- Tightened residency language:
  - Replaced broad statements like “all data stays in-region” with scoped language (e.g., “customer content is processed in the selected region” + explicit notes on what may be stored/replicated for reliability/security operations).
  - Added EMEA-friendly wording and removed absolute terms (“always”, “never”, “guarantee”) unless we can substantiate.
- Added a glossary page with definitions used in questionnaires:
  - “Customer Content”, “Operational Metadata”, “Audit Logs”, “Data Processing Region”, “Data Storage Region”, “Data Residency”, “Retention”, “Deletion”, “Subprocessors”, “Control Plane vs Data Plane”.
- Added a short “How to cite this page in questionnaires” callout with an explicit reminder: for contractual terms or exceptions, route through the evidence request process / Security.

## Notable wording decisions (to prevent over-claims)
- Avoided: “We do not store any customer data.”
  - Replaced with: scoped statements by data category + where it may exist (e.g., transient processing, logging, support artifacts) and what’s customer-configurable.
- Avoided: “All logs are region-bound.”
  - Replaced with: described audit logging separately from operational telemetry and clarified that export destinations/residency depend on deployment mode and customer configuration.
- Avoided: “GDPR compliant” / “ISO certified” / “HIPAA ready” language.
  - This PR does not introduce compliance claims; it references the security/compliance request process instead.

## Pages touched
- Enterprise Security Overview → Data handling subsection (minor edits for consistency)
- Data Retention & Deletion page (major rewrite)
- Data Residency page (major rewrite)
- New: Glossary (linked from both pages)

## Testing
- Link check + build: `pnpm docs:build` (CI)
- Manual review in preview build for table rendering + anchor links

## Follow-ups (separate work)
- Add an internal-only snippet that mirrors the glossary terms for HubSpot/CRM templates (tracked outside this PR)
- Evaluate whether the docs navigation should group these under “Security & Compliance” more prominently

## Screenshots
- N/A (text-only changes)

## Reviewer notes / convo summary
- Olga (GRC): requested we remove “guarantee” language and add a clear distinction between customer content vs operational metadata; also asked for a sentence clarifying that SOC 2 report is available under NDA via evidence request. Addressed in commit 3.
- Naomi (Product Security PM): flagged that an earlier draft implied a future feature (“region-bound control plane”)—removed; added “deployment-mode dependent” caveat instead. Addressed in commit 4.
- Markus (SE): asked for a one-paragraph “plain English” summary at the top for AEs; added “Quick interpretation” callout + link to glossary. Addressed in commit 5.
- Lukas (EMEA): requested EU residency phrasing avoid absolutes; added ‘scope of residency’ bullets and replaced “in-region storage” with “selected region for processing” where applicable. Addressed in commit 6.

## Checklist
- [x] No roadmap promises / no new product claims
- [x] Glossary added + linked
- [x] Approved by GRC + Product Security PM
- [x] CI green

Related: PM-4860 (align customer language around retention/deletion) + ENG-13942 (publish security FAQ/public-friendly overview page stubs).
